<article>

Shakeel Sobhan, Karl Sexton, with AFP, AP, Reuters | DW, August 15, 2026

At least 47 people have died and several buildings were damaged after the powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake, which was followed by dozens of aftershocks. A tsunami warning has been lifted.

A powerful earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia early on Saturday, killing at least 47 people and toppling buildings, the National Disaster Mitigation Agency said.

The epicenter of the magnitude 7.7 earthquake hit off the coast of the island of Flores at a shallow depth of 10 kilometers (6.2 miles), the US Geological Survey (USGS) said.

Shallow earthquakes (up to 70 kilometers deep) are considered more dangerous and destructive.

Tsunami waves of less than 1 meter (3 feet) were recorded in several areas of the country before the warning was lifted about three hours after the quake.

Where did the earthquake strike?

Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) recorded the first quake at 4:58 am (2158 GMT) at a depth of 15 km (9 miles), followed by dozens of aftershocks.

People rushed out onto the street as the quake struck.

Video shared on social media from Maumere, the main town in Sikka Regency on Flores Island in eastern Indonesia, showed part of a building collapsing in a cloud of dust and rubble as people screamed and ran into the street.

"Many buildings here were damaged ... I saw that the waiting room at the Pelni port terminal in Maumere had collapsed," Yohanna Embu, a resident of Sikka, a regency within East Nusa Tenggara province, told AP.

Residents evacuated, tsunami warning lifted

The initial jolt was followed by a series of aftershocks in the same area, including one of magnitude 6.1.

BMKG issued a tsunami warning for part of East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara, South Sulawesi and Southeast Sulawesi provinces, urging residents to stay away from beaches and riverbanks.

The tsunami warning was later lifted.

"We have ended (the tsunami warning) but we will keep monitoring the sea level," Wijayanto, earthquake and tsunami director at BMKG, said.

Before the tsunami warning was lifted, residents of Maumere on Flores Island were told to move to higher ground, according to AFP.

State television also showed hundreds of people evacuating in nearby Nagekeo regency.

Local TV footage showed a hospital in the district of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara Province moving patients outside.

Authorities assessing damage, casualties

The quake caused severe damage and collapsed buildings, causing power outages in cities and villages, severely hindering rescue operations.

"We are continuing to collect reports of damages and casualties, but there are communication disruptions," East Nusa Tenggara police chief Rudi Darmoko said.

Local television reports showed patients at several hospitals being evacuated from buildings as a precaution.

"Our students and nuns ran out in panic beneath a collapsing roof," Guidelbertus Tanga, rector of Ritapiret Seminary on Flores said. "At least one priest suffered a broken leg after jumping from the second floor of a building during the quake."

There were also damages reported in some part of southern Sulawesi island.

Why does Indonesia keep getting hit by major earthquakes?

Indonesia is located on the so-called "Ring of Fire," a region of heightened seismic activity in the Pacific basin that stretches from Southeast Asia to Japan.

Here are some of the biggest earthquakes to strike the region:

1992, magnitude 7: A tsunami following a strong earthquake on the southeastern island of Flores killed about 2,500 people.

2004, magnitude 9.1: A quake struck off the coast of Sumatra triggering a tsunami that killed 170,000 in Indonesia and 220,000 in several countries in the Indian Ocean.

2018, magnitude 6.9: A tremor killed more than 550 people on the islands of Lombok and Sumbawa.

2018, magnitude 7.5: A quake and a subsequent tsunami in Palu on Sulawesi island left more than 4,300 people dead or missing.
</article>

What magnitude was the earthquake?
raw: The magnitude of the earthquake was 7.7.

Ebola outbreak in DR Congo becomes deadliest in its history

KINSHASA (AFP) — The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed 2,325 people, surpassing the death toll of the 2018-2020 outbreak to become the deadliest in the country's history, public health officials said on Sunday.

DR Congo's Institute of Public Health said it had recorded 4,945 confirmed cases, including 101 in the previous 24 hours. The latest government data shows that the total number of deaths has surpassed the 2,299 deaths recorded in the 2018-2020 outbreak, which was previously the country's worst on record.

The outbreak, declared by national authorities on 15 May, is the 17th to have emerged in DR Congo since Ebola was discovered 50 years ago. It became the country's largest in terms of total confirmed cases in late July, and researchers say it may have been spreading undetected since February.

It is the fastest-growing outbreak in the known history of the virus: the world's deadliest, in West Africa in 2014-2016, took close to five months to reach 1,000 fatalities, while the current outbreak reached 2,000 deaths in under three months. The World Health Organization has said the outbreak is on track to surpass the 2014-2016 outbreak, which killed 11,325 people across Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone.

The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain. As of 19 August, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control reported 5,290 confirmed cases and 2,516 deaths, with 837 people hospitalised in Ituri, North Kivu and Haut-Uele provinces. The virus has spread to Uganda, and Europe has recorded its first imported case.

Infections among health workers continue, with at least 155 confirmed cases, including 45 deaths.

On Thursday, the UN's International Coordinating Group, led by the WHO, allocated 70,000 doses of the Ervebo vaccine, developed by Merck, to DR Congo. Ervebo is approved for the Zaire strain, used in the 2018 and 2020 DRC outbreaks, and has not been evaluated against Bundibugyo, the strain in this outbreak, so the doses will be used in a Phase 3 trial of the Zaire vaccine against Bundibugyo. The ICG had already allocated 56,000 Ervebo doses for DRC outbreaks between 2021 and July 2026.
